content.text:
Leonardo explains aerial perspective: distance, intervening air, light, shadow, and colour progressively blur forms, weaken local colours, and tint dark objects blue. Painters should simplify distant objects, preserve stronger detail and contrast in the foreground, observe atmospheric conditions, and consult nature and mirrors rather than imitate other artists. He also discusses painting, sculpture, proportion, judgment, and the limitations of reproducing binocular relief.

The architectural material surveys Sassanian, Byzantine, Armenian, Russian, Romanesque, Lombard, and Byzantine-Romanesque traditions. It traces the development of basilicas, domes, vaults, apses, towers, mosaics, and campaniles, emphasizing regional exchange. Constantine transferred the imperial government to Byzantium; Theodoric visited Rome. The Normans entered Italy, conquered Apulia from the Greeks, attacked and conquered Sicily, and later ruled southern Italy.
